title: Faraday Cages: Blocking Radio Waves
description: A Faraday enclosure is a conductive shell that blocks electromagnetic fields: incoming radio waves induce currents in the shell that cancel the field inside. Phones go silent in a sealed metal box for exactly this reason. Shielding effectiveness is measured in decibels — 60 dB means a million-fold field reduction.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Shielding Effectiveness in dB
description: Shielding effectiveness (SE) in decibels quantifies an enclosure: 20 dB is 10x field reduction, 40 dB is 100x, 80 dB is 10,000x. Real enclosures quote SE across frequency bands because shielding varies with frequency. One number without a frequency is marketing, not engineering.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: EMP Protection: MIL-STD-188-125
description: MIL-STD-188-125 specifies high-altitude EMP protection for ground facilities: shielding, filtering, and grounding that keep systems alive through the fast E1 pulse. Compliance is tested with pulse injection, not just analysis. EMP hardening is a facility discipline, not a product sticker.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: TEMPEST: The Eavesdropping Threat
description: TEMPEST is the discipline of stopping information leaking through unintentional electromagnetic emanations — monitors, cables, and processors all radiate what they are doing. Shielded enclosures, filtered power, and red/black separation are the defenses. The threat is real enough to have classified standards (NACSIM 5100A).
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Conductive Fabrics and Gaskets
description: Shielding fabrics — nickel-copper ripstop, silver mesh — make flexible enclosures: bags, curtains, and garments that block RF while staying portable. Gaskets seal the seams where rigid enclosures meet doors and panels, because a slot is an antenna. The seam is where shielding usually fails.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Mission Darkness-Style Phone Bags
description: Faraday bags for phones and laptops — Mission Darkness is the known brand — block cellular, WiFi, Bluetooth, and GPS so devices cannot be tracked or remotely wiped during transport or analysis. Forensics teams use them to preserve device state. Simple, physical, effective.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Skin Depth and Material Choice
description: Skin depth — how far fields penetrate a conductor — shrinks with frequency and conductivity: copper shields high frequencies in microns, while low frequencies need thick steel or mu-metal. Material choice follows the threat frequency. Physics picks the metal, not preference.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Apertures: Every Hole Leaks
description: Vents, cable penetrations, and display windows are apertures — and shielding degrades with the largest hole, not the best wall. Waveguide-below-cutoff vents pass air but not waves; filtered connectors pass signals but not RF. Enclosure design is aperture design.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Shielded Rooms and SCIFs
description: Shielded rooms scale the Faraday cage to buildings: SCIFs (Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities) combine RF shielding with acoustic, access, and procedural controls. Construction is inspected and accredited. A SCIF is a Faraday cage with a security policy.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Testing Shielding: The Real Proof
description: Shielding is proven by test: MIL-STD-285 and IEEE-299 methods measure SE with antennas inside and outside the enclosure across frequency sweeps. Doors get tested open-cycle because use degrades gaskets. Test reports, not datasheets, are the evidence.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Grounding the Enclosure
description: A shield must be grounded properly: single-point grounds avoid loops that re-radiate, and filters keep conducted noise off the power lines entering the cage. A floating shield is a capacitor; a looped shield is an antenna. Grounding is half the shielding art.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Portable Field Shielding
description: Field operations use portable shielding: pop-up tents, vehicle liners, and equipment covers that deploy in minutes. Compromise is explicit — portable never matches a welded room — but 40 dB in the field beats 0 dB. Mobility has a shielding budget too.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Maintenance: Shielding Degrades
description: Gaskets compress, doors wear, cables get added through new holes — shielding degrades with use and must be re-tested on schedule. Maintenance logs track every penetration. A shield is a living system, not a one-time purchase.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Designing Shielding for a Threat
description: Shielding design starts from the threat: which frequencies, what field strength, continuous or pulsed — then materials, seams, apertures, and tests follow. Over-shielding wastes money; under-shielding fails silently. The threat model is the requirements document.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: The Complete Shielding Picture
description: Ladder-top shielding: threat model, material, seams, apertures, grounding, testing, maintenance — the full discipline from physics to accredited facility. Fifteen rungs from a phone in a box to a SCIF that holds against nation-state collection.
